### **Topics Taught by Siddharth**

Siddharth extensively covered foundational and advanced concepts related to context windows, token limits, and prompt engineering, often integrating them into practical RAG system design.

*   **Prompt Engineering & Context Management:**
    *   **Core Concept**: Siddharth emphasized that LLMs require specific prompts and instructions to connect with retrieved information effectively, highlighting the necessity of context in generating relevant responses. He asked Himaya, "How are you connecting your rack system to the LLM?" and corrected her when she only mentioned "prompt and instructions," clarifying that "if you give only prompt and instructions, then how will it know what information it got from Raja?" [2026-07-22, Page 7-8 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: This was crucial for trainees to understand how to bridge the gap between retrieved data (RAG) and the LLM's generative capabilities, moving beyond simple instructions to structured information feeding.

*   **Token Limits & Context Window Optimization:**
    *   **Core Concept**: Siddharth directly addressed the issue of token limits and context heavy inputs, particularly in the context of large datasets like Excel files. He challenged Ganesh's approach of converting an entire Excel file into a database schema for LLM access, stating, "Basically, this Excel file may be like there may be thousands of... rows and columns right there in this so if we are passing the JSON file like JSON of thousands and all to directly to LLM will it be like it will be context heavy right and the tokens and all will be Very much, yeah" [2026-07-14, Page 7-9 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: He stressed the practical implications of context size on performance and cost, driving the need for efficient data representation and retrieval strategies.
    *   **Re-ranking for Token Efficiency**: Siddharth guided Dakshinya on optimizing context windows by using re-ranking to send only relevant chunks to the LLM. He pointed out, "Every time you are sending 10 chunks to the model, irrespective of whether they are relevant or irrelevant. Is it correct or not?" and then clarified, "So instead of sending top 10 every time, you will only send the top things that are actually relevant from your re-ranker" [2026-07-22, Page 11-12 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: This taught trainees how to reduce unnecessary token usage, thereby improving efficiency and reducing computational costs by being selective with the information fed into the LLM.

*   **Context Window as a Fundamental Concept:**
    *   **Core Concept**: Siddharth explicitly defined and provided resources for understanding context windows. He stated, "Take a look at this file, so that you guys understand what is context window and problem for the last time" [2026-07-28, Page 17 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: This ensured a foundational understanding of how LLMs process and retain information within a given interaction, which is critical for effective prompt design and RAG system architecture.

*   **Context Engineering Engine within RAG Architecture:**
    *   **Core Concept**: As part of system design, Siddharth detailed the "context engineering engine" as a crucial component of the RAG system architecture (System Two). He outlined the "prompt builder, context engineering engine, reusable rerun" as key elements [2026-08-17, Page 4-5 — Siddharth Saminathan].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: This placed context management within a broader architectural framework, showing its role in a scalable and modular RAG system.

*   **Practical Implications of Token Limits (Himaya's Agents):**
    *   **Core Concept**: Himaya mentioned "token limits and all" as a reason for changing her code, indicating that Siddharth's discussions around these constraints influenced her design decisions for her agents [2026-08-18, Page 1-2 — Himaya Perumal].
    *   **Why Emphasized**: This demonstrates that Siddharth instilled an awareness of token limits as a practical constraint that directly impacts implementation choices and system design.
